blueprint_refs: objective: ordered sequences of (POI_location_id, time) visits, matching empirical temporal patterns
action_decision_policy: "decide whether to end day based on time and fatigue/time_budget"
stop-count-mismatch-day-truncation-and-n.error_identification: Simulated days have substantially wrong number of stops (mean absolute error ~1.64 stops/day; KL ~0.40).
stop-count-mismatch-day-truncation-and-n.root_cause_analysis: The simulator samples a stop count (n_stops) but then can end early via a time-based hazard gate and also stops when t reaches day end; it never plans an explicit end-of-day home return or guarantees completion of sampled stops. This disconnect between sampled stop-count distribution and realized execution produces stop-count divergence.
stop-count-mismatch-day-truncation-and-n.correct_approach: Make realized stop counts consistent with sampled stop counts: (1) generate a daily plan with target number of stops and time windows, then execute it; (2) only allow early termination as an explicit model component (fatigue/time_budget) calibrated to match observed early-stop behavior; (3) optionally add an explicit final 'home' visit (if home exists in data) or enforce day-end closure after last activity rather than truncation mid-plan.
stop-count-mismatch-day-truncation-and-n.key_insight: If you sample a quantity that is evaluated (e.g., stops/day), enforce it during rollout or model the reasons it deviates and calibrate that deviation directly.

blueprint_refs: policy_form: "sample next coarse_category ... conditioned on time-of-day and day_type"

evidence.metrics: tod_jsd_avg≈0.130; some categories very high (e.g., Shop & Service ~0.32, Food ~0.21)

category-time-of-day-jsd-high-missing-ti.error_identification: Time-of-day visit start distributions by coarse category are poorly matched (average JSD ~0.13; specific categories much worse).
category-time-of-day-jsd-high-missing-ti.root_cause_analysis: Category choice is influenced by time-of-day only via multiplying transition probs by minute-bin probabilities from per-agent/per-global histograms at the current t, but the simulator does not explicitly model (a) departure time distributions by category, (b) dwell-time interactions that shift subsequent arrival times, or (c) day-type conditioned category mixtures beyond transitions. This is weaker than the blueprint’s “schedule constraints” and “time-of-day departure patterns” components, making it hard to hit per-category timing targets.
category-time-of-day-jsd-high-missing-ti.correct_approach: Introduce an explicit schedule model: sample (category, target_start_time) pairs for the day from fitted per-category time-of-day priors (conditioned on day_type), then choose POIs/transitions consistent with those target times (e.g., penalize |arrive_time - target_start_time| in utility). Keep transition priors as a secondary term instead of the sole driver of timing.
category-time-of-day-jsd-high-missing-ti.key_insight: To match time-of-day patterns, timing must be a first-class variable (planned or strongly constrained), not just a weak multiplicative prior in a Markov transition.

blueprint_refs: policy_form: utility combines personal POI affinity, global attractiveness, distance decay, optional recency penalty
poi-recall-low-candidate-set-and-utility.error_identification: Top-K POI recall is low (~0.22), indicating the simulator misses many agents’ frequent validation POIs.
poi-recall-low-candidate-set-and-utility.root_cause_analysis: The candidate generation draws many POIs (up to ~40) and uses a large global transition topk (best ~157) filtered by category; then utilities rely on fixed weights for affinity/popularity/transition and only calibrate temperature. Because weights like w_personal_poi_affinity and w_global_poi_popularity are not calibrated (fixed at 1.0), calibration cannot shift probability mass toward anchor POIs enough to improve recall, and large candidate sets dilute selection.
poi-recall-low-candidate-set-and-utility.correct_approach: Expose and calibrate POI utility weights that the blueprint lists (w_personal_poi_affinity, w_global_poi_popularity, and possibly a separate weight for POI-transition prior). Also reduce candidate set size or make it adaptive: always include top-N anchor POIs and only a small exploration tail. Consider adding a recency penalty term (blueprint optional) to prevent repetitive non-anchor churn while preserving anchor revisits.
poi-recall-low-candidate-set-and-utility.key_insight: If a metric targets specific items (top-K POIs), ensure the model has calibratable knobs that can concentrate probability mass on those items; temperature alone can’t fix systematic misspecification.

blueprint_refs: calibratable_parameters: travel_time_speed_kmph (used to match inter-event time gaps distribution)
dwell_time_params_by_coarse_category: "only arrival timestamps are observed; dwell inferred/latent"
travel-time-speed-calibrates-to-unrealis.error_identification: Calibration selects very high effective travel speed (~74 km/h), suggesting the simulator is compensating for timing misfit via unrealistic travel times.
travel-time-speed-calibrates-to-unrealis.root_cause_analysis: Dwell-time fitting subtracts an estimated travel time using a fixed DEFAULT_DWELL_FIT_SPEED_KMPH (30 km/h), while simulation travel time uses a calibrated speed. This mismatch means dwell-time parameters are learned under one travel-time assumption but used under another, encouraging calibration to push speed high to reconcile arrival times without re-fitting dwell accordingly.
travel-time-speed-calibrates-to-unrealis.correct_approach: Couple dwell/travel estimation: either (1) fit dwell-time parameters with the same speed used in simulation (iterate: estimate speed → refit dwell → recalibrate), or (2) treat dwell-time params and travel speed jointly in the calibration objective by recomputing dwell-time model per sampled speed (expensive but consistent). At minimum, log and compare implied dwell distributions vs observed inter-event gaps on validation to ensure plausibility.
travel-time-speed-calibrates-to-unrealis.key_insight: Do not fit latent components (dwell) using a fixed decomposition if another decomposed component (travel speed) is later calibrated—otherwise calibration will push to implausible extremes.

blueprint_refs: calibratable_parameters: "candidate_set_topk_from_transition_graph" = "How many next-POI candidates to consider from the empirical mobility graph before adding exploration"

evidence.metrics: best candidate_set_topk_from_transition_graph=157 while final candidates are capped ~12-40

candidate-set-topk-from-transition-graph.error_identification: The calibrated parameter candidate_set_topk_from_transition_graph takes large values, but actual candidate list size is capped (~40), so the parameter’s effect is muted/non-identifiable.
candidate-set-topk-from-transition-graph.root_cause_analysis: In _candidate_pois, topk controls how many neighbors are scanned from the transition graph, but then candidates are filtered by category and the final set is capped by target_total (12–40). With many categories, few graph neighbors pass the filter, and the cap dominates; calibration can’t reliably use this parameter to shape behavior as intended by the blueprint.
candidate-set-topk-from-transition-graph.correct_approach: Make candidate_set_topk_from_transition_graph directly control the number of graph-derived candidates included (after category filtering), and separate it from the overall cap. For example: include up to K graph neighbors that match the target category, then add exploration candidates up to an independent exploration cap.
candidate-set-topk-from-transition-graph.key_insight: A calibratable parameter must have a clear, monotonic effect on the generated behavior; otherwise optimization drifts and you get misleading ‘best’ values.

blueprint_refs: place dynamic_states: "Increment when resident arrives; decrement when resident departs"
co_location_contact: overlap of time windows within time_bin

evidence.metrics: interaction_summaries present; POI.current_occupancy is set per bin then reset (no dynamic simulation loop)

colocation-implementation-is-summary-onl.error_identification: Occupancy/contact are computed as post-hoc summaries, not as part of the event-driven place state updates described in the blueprint.
colocation-implementation-is-summary-onl.root_cause_analysis: The code resets POI.current_occupancy and sets it to the bin occupancy during aggregation, then resets again; it does not maintain occupancy increment/decrement on resident arrivals/departures during simulation. This limits extensibility for congestion/crowding feedback or any contact-dependent mechanisms.
colocation-implementation-is-summary-onl.correct_approach: If occupancy is intended to influence choice or be a true dynamic state, update POI.current_occupancy during simulation as events occur (increment on arrival, schedule decrement on departure). Keep the post-hoc bin-based contact counting, but derive it from the same event stream to avoid two inconsistent representations.
colocation-implementation-is-summary-onl.key_insight: If a state variable is defined as dynamic in the spec, update it in the simulator’s core loop; post-hoc recomputation is fine for metrics but shouldn’t masquerade as state.

evidence.metrics: execution succeeded, but module ends with main() unguarded

main-executes-on-import-side-effect.error_identification: The script calls main() at import time, which can break reuse/testing and some harnesses that import modules.
main-executes-on-import-side-effect.root_cause_analysis: At the end of the file, main() is called without an `if __name__ == "__main__":` guard.
main-executes-on-import-side-effect.correct_approach:
Wrap the call in the standard guard:
- replace trailing `main()` with:
  `if __name__ == "__main__":
      main()`
main-executes-on-import-side-effect.key_insight: Never execute CLI entrypoints on import; always guard main to keep code composable and testable.
